entries.title: Psalms 25:1
segments: This is the first of the alphabetic psalms; that is, psalms where the verses correspond to the twenty-two letters of the Hebrew alphabet, each beginning with one of its letters in regular order.  As the natural result of their structure, such psalms consist rather of collections of pious thought and sentiments, than of connected trains of discourse.

entries.title: Psalms 25:4
segments: Right views of ourselves will lead us to feel our need of being taught of God, and habitually to seek help from him.

entries.title: Psalms 25:7
segments: Sins committed in youth may, even when repented of, greatly imbitter the comforts of age, and be felt in their effects to the end of life.

entries.title: Psalms 25:8
segments: In the way; the way of truth and of duty God will teach to all sinners who feel their need of being taught, and are disposed to learn of him.

entries.title: Psalms 25:10
segments: The paths of the Lord; the ways in which he deals with his people are wise, faithful, and gracious, however trying and mysterious they may sometimes be.

entries.title: Psalms 25:11
segments: The greatness of one's iniquities is no insuperable barrier to their being pardoned, and may, in some cases, be pleaded as a reason why the Lord, to the honor of his abounding grace, should show mercy.

entries.title: Psalms 25:14
segments:
The secret of the Lord; his intimate friendship, with the blessedness and prosperity which it gives. 
 
The blessedness of serving God is known only by being experienced, and can be known in no other way.

entries.title: Psalms 25:15
segments: Out of the net; deliver him from his enemies.

entries.title: Psalms 25:18
segments:
My sins; the cause of his troubles. 
 
Sin is viewed by the penitent soul as the cause of all his troubles; and he is more anxious to be delivered from it than from all outward distresses.

entries.title: Psalms 25:22
segments:
Israel; the people of God. 
 
The benevolent soul desires and prays for the choicest of heaven's blessings not only on itself, but on all who love and serve the Lord, throughtout the earth.
